overview: White offers the b-pawn with 3.b4 after 2...e6, hoping to deflect the c5 pawn and build a big d4/e4 centre. After 3...cxb4 4.a3 White gets the centre and open a-file, but Black can keep the pawn with ...d5 or ...Nf6 and have the better structure. White's compensation is considered insufficient at the top.

white_ideas.idea: Play a3, axb4 and d4 to build a strong centre
Use the open a-file and quick development
Aim for e5 and kingside play

black_ideas.idea: Take on b4 and hit the centre with ...d5 or ...Nf6
Return the pawn if needed for equal play

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 centre against ...e6 and open b-file

character.notes: Early wing pawn sacrifice with an open centre and tactical play.

gambit.notes: White gives the b-pawn for centre control and development, and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Black can keep the pawn with ...d5, and engines prefer Black.

structure.notes: Every Sicilian leaves a half-open file; White has the open a-file, Black the c-file.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose the Wing Gambit against the Sicilian.

level.notes: Plans are straightforward but dubious, so not for beginners.
